summary: Intermittent upstream backpressure misperceived as model slowdown during morning ingest window
description:
Issue summary:
Medlytics reported recurring long-tail inference latencies and streaming timeouts each weekday between 08:10 and 09:00 local time. Customer perceived the model as 'hanging' or timing out for single-request generations. Initial triage showed elevated queueing and a large number of near-simultaneous reconnects from the customer's ingestion pipeline.

Impact:
- Several customer endpoints experienced 5-15% error rates (stream disconnects / 499s from customer SDK) during the window.
- Business impact: delayed processing of urgent clinical notes leading to batch reprocessing and customer downtime for parts of the morning ingest.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool assigned to Medlytics, prod/us-east-1, autoscaling enabled with burst capacity.
- Customer is on an event-driven ingestion system that issues many short streaming requests (avg 1.8s) at scale during morning startup.

Expected behavior:
- Short streaming requests should complete with median latency < 450ms and failure rate < 0.1% during normal load.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent long-tail latency spikes (p99 > 4s), increased streaming disconnects, and a high volume of repeated connect attempts from the client during the window.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a dedicated customer pool with similar concurrency limits to Medlytics (dedicated GPUs, default burst policy).
2) Simulate morning ingest: send 6k short streaming generation requests over 3 minutes (average ~33rps burst).
3) Use a client that retries immediately on perceived timeout (simple exponential backoff with short initial delay and no jitter).
4) Observe serving-runtime queue depth, batcher saturation, and any 429/soft-quota signals.

Notes: reproducer attached in linked PR and support runbook.
logs:
Sample relevant logs (redacted):
- api-gateway: 2026-03-10T08:12:05Z [WARN] conn 0x7f3a drop: stream closed by client after 2500ms
- serving-runtime: 2026-03-10T08:12:06Z [INFO] pool=medlytics deduped-batches=18 active-batches=5 queued-requests=387 kernel-select=avx2
- scheduler: 2026-03-10T08:12:06Z [WARN] soft-quota-hit customer=medlytics window=60s tokens-left=0 next-unblock=2026-03-10T08:12:39Z
- sdk (customer): 2026-03-10T08:12:07Z [INFO] retry_attempt=3 event=client-timeout observed=408
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: model regression or kernel stall.
Findings:
- No model-side regressions found (commit history & perf tests clean).
- Autoscaling behaved as expected, GPUs not saturated by compute, but request queue length spiked during the burst.
- The dedicated pool enforces a soft per-customer burst window to protect noisy neighbors. When the burst tokens were exhausted, requests entered a queue and received a soft-429 signal; customer SDK interpreted early streaming disconnects/timeouts as failures and retried quickly.
- Rapid retries increased instantaneous concurrency and caused batcher saturation and head-of-line blocking: longer tails for small requests that share batch windows.
- Observed correlation: peaks in SDK retry rate precede the longest queue depths by ~8-12s.
- Reproducible with local load generator when client retry policy lacked jitter and did not respect 429/Retry-After.

Relevant cross-references: Slack #support thread (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/G12345/p1674000), related incident SUP-331878 (soft-quota window behavior), and PR to add queue metrics (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2184).
resolution_notes:
Short-term mitigations applied (2026-03-10 12:30Z):
- Increased soft-burst tokens for Medlytics dedicated pool for morning window by 25% for 48h.
- Updated rate-window logging to emit detailed per-customer queue depth every 10s (helped verify mitigation).
- Escalated to SDK team: requested immediate guidance to customer to change client retry policy to honor 429/Retry-After and add jitter.

Medium-term fixes deployed (2026-03-11 to 2026-03-12):
- Serving-runtime: adjusted batcher scheduling to prioritize short, low-token-length requests during small-request bursts (deploy: serving-runtime v1.23.1).
- Scheduler: tuned soft-quota window algorithm to smooth token replenishment when repeated short requests are detected in a narrow time window (deploy: scheduler v0.9.7).
- SDK: released advisory and patch (redwood-sdk v1.4.2) with recommended retry templates and a client-side circuit breaker sample.

Customer communication:
- Notified Medlytics on 2026-03-11 with the changes and recommended client changes. Customer confirmed reduced error rates during subsequent windows (post-change p99 latency fell from ~4.2s to ~0.7s; stream disconnects down to 0.3%).

Follow-ups:
- Engineering to monitor next two weeks of morning ingest windows and consider permanent quota plan change if traffic pattern persists.
- Create a new runbook entry about coordinated quota + client retry patterns.
